no-covid-19-pandemic-occurs.summary: In this world, the voters I interviewed lean 4.1 points further toward Trump than the same people did in 2020 as it was. Trump wins, 314–224. The closest call is Arizona, which holds for Biden by 0.3 points. Trump wins in 93 of 100 draws. Extremely low confidence. The interviews point the other way from the historical record.
assumptions: The pandemic and its economic and political effects are removed from the campaign; voters judge the President on the pre-2020 economy and other issues, and voting proceeds by ordinary rules.
howIGotThis: What changed: The coronavirus never spreads worldwide, so 2020 passes without a pandemic, lockdowns or a pandemic recession.

What historians found (12 findings, strong evidence): Trump's approval peaked near 49% before the pandemic and fell to about 39-42% by summer, ending at 46%. Economic approval dropped 15 points. Turnout rose sharply in 2020 (about 5-7 points) amid mail-voting expansion, but the notes cannot separate pandemic effects from polarization. Incumbents under 48% approval have not won.
The numbers: the 2020 census counts and certified returns; every draw reproduces 2020 exactly before the change.
How sure: I reran it 100 times with different population and parameter draws.
Extremely low confidence: The interviews point the other way from the historical record.
